summary: Fairbanks Police report that Hunter Joseph Ptacek, 19, was arrested on Nov. 1 on a charge of driving under the influence on College Road; the arrest was added to the department's bulletin for Nov. 1 after this report was first compiled on Tuesday morning. Alaska State Troopers report that Justin West, 35, of Tok was arrested on Nov. 1 on two counts of assault in the second degree and one count of assault in the fourth degree and was taken to the Fairbanks jail. Troopers reported no incidents inside the Fairbanks area on Nov. 2, and the troopers' page for Nov. 3 had not been published when this report was compiled. Fairbanks Police reported no arrests for either Nov. 2 or the early hours of Nov. 3. The Alaska Court System's public case database was unavailable throughout the morning and was still unavailable at about 4:50 a.m., so no hearing results, new filings or case updates for Nov. 3 could be read and the open-case list below is as it stood on Nov. 2. The court's weekly criminal filings report, which was available, covers Oct. 27 to Nov. 2 and lists 38 cases filed at Fairbanks, four at Nenana, two at Delta Junction and none at Healy; it includes all ten of the cases filed at Fairbanks on Nov. 2 that were reported here yesterday. Eleven case numbers within the range the report prints are missing from it, all of them files opened at Fairbanks on Oct. 28 that name no defendant.

entries.title: DUI arrest: Hunter Joseph Ptacek
body: Hunter Joseph Ptacek, 19, was arrested on a charge of driving under the influence with a blood alcohol level of .08 percent or more, recorded by police as a misdemeanor. 1300 block of College Road, Fairbanks, Nov. 1 at 1:57 a.m.; Fairbanks Police. Police case 26003330.

A court file was opened at Fairbanks the same day, case 4FA-26-02208CR. It records one count as a charging document pending or not filed and states no degree of offense, so no charge class comes from the court. Arraignment Nov. 6.

entries.title: Assault arrest: Justin West
body: Justin West, 35, of Tok, was arrested on two counts of assault in the second degree and one count of assault in the fourth degree, as recorded by troopers. Assault in the second degree is a Class B felony under Alaska law, punishable by up to 10 years; no court file could be read, so no charge as filed is stated here.
A residence in Tok, Nov. 1 at about 8:40 p.m.; Alaska State Troopers. Troopers say they responded to a request for a welfare check and that the investigation resulted in his arrest.
Troopers say he was taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center and held pending arraignment.

sources.label: Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, Nov. 2

entries.title: Alaska's public court case database was unavailable on Tuesday morning
body: CourtView, the Alaska Court System's public online case database at records.courts.alaska.gov, returned the message "The service is unavailable" to every request made on Nov. 3 between about 3:20 a.m. and about 4:50 a.m. Four different pages on the site, including the search page, returned the same message.

The site is the only public place where an individual Alaska criminal case file can be looked up by case number or by name. Court calendars, charges, hearing dates and docket entries are published there and nowhere else.
The court system's two weekly report files, which list criminal charges filed and cases disposed across the state, were available and were read.
Because the case database could not be read, no hearing results, new filings or case updates from Nov. 3 are reported here. The list of open cases below is as it stood on Nov. 2.
